name: West Linn
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in West Linn, OR 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in West Linn, OR: the Light Up the Night holiday parade, the Historic Willamette tree lighting, hot cocoa, carols and nearby train rides.
lede: West Linn does Christmas in the Historic Willamette business district, where a holiday parade, a Main Street tree lighting with hot cocoa and carols, and a decorating contest among local shops bring families onto Willamette Falls Drive each winter.
celebrates: The City of West Linn Parks and Recreation Department hosts its annual "Light Up the Night" Holiday Parade in the Historic Willamette Main Street area, along Willamette Falls Drive. Historic Willamette Main Street, the downtown nonprofit, holds its Main Street Holiday Tree Lighting outside the Ale and Cider House, with hot cocoa and cider, a Holiday Decorating Contest for local businesses and carol singing. Willamette Christian Church also hosts a tree lighting of its own. Families can pick the parade, a tree lighting or both, and Willamette Falls Drive is closed to cars while the events are on.
lastyear: In 2025 Historic Willamette Main Street planned its Main Street Holiday Tree Lighting for Saturday, November 29, at 6 pm outside the Ale and Cider House at 1720 Willamette Falls Drive. The tree was donated by Holy Star Farm, and the West Linn Chorus was scheduled to provide festive music. The event page asked neighbors to bring donations for the West Linn Food Pantry to help restock its shelves for the winter, and a songbook was posted so families could sing along.
facts: West Linn grew from the pioneer town of Linn City, which Robert Moore built near Willamette Falls in the 1840s and renamed in 1845 for his friend Dr. Lewis F. Linn, a U.S. senator. In 1913 West Oregon City, Bolton, Sunset and Willamette Heights joined to form the city, and the founders chose to honor Linn City. In 2024 the Main Street tree was lit at 6:10 pm, and five minutes later the Main Street lights along Willamette Falls Drive came alive.
trains: WES Commuter Rail, TriMet's weekday rush-hour train, stops in nearby Tualatin and Wilsonville, and MAX light rail connects in Portland, so families can plan a train day around a West Linn visit. Close by, the Willamette Shore Trolley in Lake Oswego runs vintage trolley trips along the Willamette River toward Portland. In Portland, the Oregon Rail Heritage Center runs the Holiday Express steam train, and the Washington Park and Zoo Railway runs at the Oregon Zoo.

faq: Where is the West Linn Christmas tree lighting?

Historic Willamette Main Street lights its Main Street Holiday Tree outside the Ale and Cider House, 1720 Willamette Falls Drive, in the Historic Willamette business district. Hot cocoa and cider are served nearby, and the night ends with the Holiday Decorating Contest winners and carols. Willamette Falls Drive is closed to cars during the event.
Who hosts the West Linn holiday parade?

The City of West Linn Parks and Recreation Department hosts the annual "Light Up the Night" Holiday Parade in the Historic Willamette Main Street area. The city asks neighbors not to park on Willamette Falls Drive along the route, because parking there closes early and cars left on the route can be towed.
How does Santa light the tree in West Linn?

The city's parade page says Santa is the very last entry in the parade. When children see his sleigh, families can walk behind the parade and follow Santa to the tree at the Ale and Cider House. He lights the tree after the parade has finished its route.
Can kids see Christmas lights in downtown West Linn?

Yes. The Historic Willamette Main Street tree lighting also brings on the Main Street tree lights along Willamette Falls Drive, as it did at the 2024 event. The decorating contest recognizes local businesses for decorated wreaths, windows and outdoor displays.
Is there a train near West Linn for kids?

Yes. WES Commuter Rail, a weekday rush-hour train, stops in nearby Tualatin and Wilsonville. The Willamette Shore Trolley runs vintage trolley trips from Lake Oswego toward Portland, and Portland's Oregon Rail Heritage Center runs the Holiday Express steam train each December.
